text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Government to create some 50,000 jobs for the young in the public sector from September, measure is expected to cost around two billion francs. Decree to be signed shortly is expected to allocate some eleven billion francs to social measures.
-- GEC plans to pull out of Franco-British conglomerate GEC Alsthom, which may eventually be listed on the stock exchange.

-- Pension funds will be launched in France. Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn says government to hold talks with insurers, bankers and labour unions on modifying pension fund law passed by previous centre-right government.
-- Government seeks to slow down layoff procedures, notably in the automobile sector, as called for by the Communist party.
-- According to a union source, arms manufacturer Giat Industries needs a 4.5 billion francs recapitalisation per year through the year 2000.
-- Re-insurance firm Sfac economists expect 1998 growth above three percent.
-- Treasury announces method for converting French state bond into euros, via rounding to the nearest euro and payment of a cash rebate when needed.
-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn does not rule out an increase in wealth tax this year, as announced in the Socialist election platform.
-- Hotels groups Hyatt and Hilton may be interested in buying hotel group Royal Monceau, placed under legal administration since the spring of 1996.
-- Union at British Airways' French units TAT and Air Liberte expects further brief strikes over flight attendants' status.
-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn says France is "ready for the euro".
